page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.E3.128 is a bare-metal server powered by AMD EPYC 7742 processors built on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware deployment includes 128 physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz. With simultaneous multithreading active at two threads per core, the host exposes 256 dedicated vCPUs. System memory is provisioned at 2048 GB, establishing an allocation of 8 GB of RAM per vCPU without hardware-level hypervisor overhead.

Storage configuration on this server includes no local NVMe or SATA storage arrays, requiring persistent file systems and operating systems to rely on network-attached block volumes. The server contains no GPU hardware acceleration modules. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, and the bare-metal architecture grants direct access to the entire physical CPU socket and memory subsystem.

The dense core count and two-terabyte memory footprint make BM.Standard.E3.128 applicable for large in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, big data processing frameworks, and high-concurrency batch processing. Workloads demanding high IOPS local scratch storage or GPU acceleration will require external storage architecture adjustments or alternative accelerated hardware classes.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.E3.128 is a bare-metal server configuration powered by dual AMD EPYC 7742 processors on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 128 physical cores and 256 dedicated vCPUs running at 2.25 GHz, paired with 2048 GB of system RAM for an allocation of 8 GB per vCPU. The server includes no local disk storage, necessitating network-attached storage for system volumes, and it contains no GPU accelerators. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provided. Operating as a bare-metal node, the instance avoids hypervisor virtualization overhead, granting full access to hardware execution units and system memory. This resource profile is engineered to support memory-heavy enterprise software, large in-memory caching solutions, large-scale distributed analytics, and dense multi-threaded server workloads requiring substantial memory capacity per thread.
